name: CarMax, Inc.

profile.description: CarMax is the largest retailer of used vehicles in the United States, operating an omni-channel platform that lets customers buy and sell cars online, in-store, or through a hybrid of both, plus CarMax Auto Finance (CAF), which originates and services auto loans. FY2026 (ended February 2026) revenue was $25.9B (-1.8% YoY) with net income of $247M. Under CEO Keith Barr (appointed March 2026, former CEO of InterContinental Hotels Group), the turnaround is gaining traction: Q2 FY2027 (ended August 31, 2026) revenue rose 19.5% to $7.9B, combined used units rose 14.7% and diluted EPS rose 81% to $1.16. A Strategic Update is scheduled for November 3, 2026. Market cap approximately $7.9B.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): CarMax's omni-channel build-out (online buying/selling, instant offers, home delivery) was a meaningful extension, but the core buy-recondition-sell model is largely unchanged since 1993 [1][4]. AI Deployment (2/2): CarMax is shipping customer-facing AI at scale: the Skye virtual assistant and agentic Skye 2.0 handle tens of thousands of conversations weekly, it became the first U.S. car retailer with buying and selling inside the ChatGPT app store (February 2026), and Sierra AI voice agents were deployed on inbound sales calls in May 2026; executives tie AI and tech investments to at least $150M of cost savings [5][10]. Market Share (2/2): CarMax is the #1 used-vehicle retailer in the U.S., and Q2 FY2027 combined unit sales grew 14.7% to 387,735, a share-gaining quarter [1]. Pipeline (1/2): Management has a $200M exit-rate SG&A savings target by end of FY2027 and a Strategic Update on November 3, but no named next-generation products with revenue visibility [1]. R&D Intensity (0/1): CarMax reports no R&D line; technology spend sits in SG&A [2].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): CarMax's purpose of driving integrity through honest, transparent, no-haggle car buying has been consistent since 1993 and addresses a real consumer pain point, but it is clear rather than transformative [7]. Community Impact (1/2): The 2026 Responsibility Report documents the CarMax Foundation's community giving and achievement of a 50% cut in Scope 1 and 2 emissions versus the 2018 baseline, which is solid general philanthropy rather than distinctive impact [7]. Employee Retention (1/2): CarMax has been named to Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For for 21 consecutive years, but no hard turnover data is disclosed and a CEO termination in late 2025 disrupted continuity [4]. Insider Buying (2/2): In June 2026 CEO Keith Barr bought 9,400 shares at about $53.01 (~$498K), joined by directors Mark O'Neil (4,800 shares at $52.36), Peter Bensen (2,500 at $52.20), Sona Chawla (2,000 at $53.39) and Marcella Shinder (574 at $52.01), a broad open-market buying cluster with no offsetting sales reported [6].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored (Growth, 10 weight units): D/E of 286.6% sits just inside the 300% floor (0.06), because most debt is non-recourse auto-loan securitization funding for CAF [3][2]. ROE of 4.7% scores 0.31 (2x weight) and profit margin of 1.0% scores 0.05, reflecting thin used-car retail economics [3]. Revenue growth of 17.7% YoY (Q2 FY2027 +19.5%) scores 1.0, the 5yr revenue CAGR of 6.4% (FY2021 $18.95B to FY2026 $25.88B) scores 0.76 (2x), forward P/E of 15.6 scores 1.0, and FMP's forward PEG of 1.43 scores 0.78 (2x) [1][2][3]. Weighted sum 5.83/10 rounds to 6; liquidity clears the floor easily at ~2.5M shares/day x $55.58.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9 — PROTECTED): CarMax's value chain is physical — sourcing vehicles, inspection and reconditioning, a national store and logistics footprint, test drives, and a captive finance arm with $1.9B of annual interest income — none of which AI can substitute [2][1]. The exposure is at the discovery and pricing layer: AI shopping agents (including ChatGPT, where CarMax has chosen to be present first) could compress price transparency and lead-generation advantages, and commentators flag reliability risk in handing a major customer touchpoint to LLMs [5]. AI Opportunity (0/1): AI is clearly an internal enabler (Skye 2.0, Sierra voice agents, a $150M+ savings target), but CarMax does not report quantifiable AI revenue [5][10].

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens, CarMax was founded on a genuine cause — taking the fear and haggling out of buying a used car — and has built a durable people-first culture, but the last two years show a company reacting to the quarter: a stock collapse, the termination of the long-tenured CEO, and a turnaround framed around SG&A cuts. Insider buying and early unit growth under Keith Barr are encouraging, but the cause has not yet been re-articulated beyond cost and efficiency.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): The 1993 founding idea of honest, no-haggle used-car buying was genuinely countercultural and still differentiates CarMax [7]. But today's strategic language centres on SG&A savings, unit growth and retail margins rather than a future state worth sacrificing for, so the cause reads more as a brand promise than a driving purpose [1].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): 21 consecutive years on Fortune's 100 Best Companies to Work For is real evidence of a stable, people-first culture [4]. However, the November 2025 termination of CEO Bill Nash and an aggressive $200M cost-savings program create uncertainty that keeps this at adequate rather than exceptional [1][4].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): CarMax has historically treated online-native rivals like Carvana as a mirror, responding by building its own instant-offer, home-delivery and digital financing capabilities rather than simply competing on price [1][5]. Being first to put buying and selling inside ChatGPT shows a learn-and-adapt posture toward new channels [5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): CarMax evolved from a pure big-box store model to a full omni-channel retailer and is now layering agentic AI onto the customer journey [5]. These are meaningful but incremental adaptations; the company has not reinvented its core model.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): The CEO and five directors bought shares in the open market in June 2026 when the stock was near multi-year lows, and the company kept investing in technology through a down cycle [6][5]. Offsetting that, the turnaround is primarily cost-driven and the board's 2025 CEO change was a reaction to stock-price pressure [4].

investment_thesis: CarMax's turnaround under Keith Barr is showing up in the numbers: Q2 FY2027 revenue rose 19.5% to $7.9B, combined used units grew 14.7%, diluted EPS jumped 81% to $1.16, CAF income rose 32% on lower loss provisions, and SG&A per unit fell 8.8% as the $200M savings program lands [1]. At $55.58 the stock trades at 15.6x forward earnings, 1.25x book and roughly 6.9x price-to-free-cash-flow, management plans to restart buybacks in Q3, and the CEO plus five directors bought stock in June around $52-53 [3][2][6]. AI deployment (Skye 2.0, Sierra voice agents, a ChatGPT app) gives a credible path to further cost leverage [5].
thesis_continued: The bear case: net margins of about 1% and ROE under 5% leave little cushion, and D/E of 287% means CAF credit performance (loss provisions, securitization funding costs) can swing earnings sharply [3][2]. The Q2 rebound came against a weak prior-year comparison and part of the margin gain came from a lower loan-loss provision rather than retail profitability [1]. A securities class action over 2025 disclosures is pending, and Carvana continues to take digital share [9]. The November 3 Strategic Update is a binary near-term event.
key_catalysts: November 3, 2026 Strategic Update: new medium-term targets for units, retail GPU and SG&A leverage under CEO Keith Barr
Resumption of share repurchases in Q3 FY2027 with ~147M shares outstanding and ~$8B market cap
Delivery of the $200M exit-rate SG&A savings by end of FY2027 plus $150M+ AI/technology-driven savings
Continued CAF loss-provision normalization lifting finance income (+32% YoY in Q2)
key_risks: Credit deterioration in the CAF subprime and near-prime loan book forcing higher loss provisions
Retail gross profit per unit pressure (management guides FY2027 retail margins down up to ~$200/unit) as AI shopping tools increase price transparency
Carvana and franchise dealers taking online used-vehicle share
Securities class action covering June-September 2025 disclosures
